idiom_name: class with a #private field and a static parse (runtime brand)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no static types, so the newtype degrades to a runtime brand: a class whose #private field can only be set by the constructor, instances that pass instanceof, and a static parse as the single validating entry point. The classic OO wrapper survives essentially unchanged - constructor, accessor, explicit valueOf/toJSON - and Object.freeze removes the last mutation path. TypeScript's branded types cover typed call sites at compile time, but this runtime object is what still protects untyped callers, configuration objects and data coming from JSON.parse.
pitfalls: Brands evaporate at boundaries: JSON.stringify(id) yields {} unless toJSON is defined, and structuredClone/Object.assign do not rebuild a UserId from a primitive.
Coercion hooks re-admit the primitive: valueOf/toString make id + 1 and id > 'x' legal, so add them only where the domain wants arithmetic.
instanceof fails across realms, iframes and duplicated module instances (dual-package hazard); use a Symbol.for-based brand or re-validate through parse at those boundaries.
